question_text: The diffusion coefficient of nickel in an austenitic (fcc structure) stainless steel is $10^{-22} \mathrm{~m}^2 / \mathrm{s}$ at $500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}^2 / \mathrm{s}$ at $1,000^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Calculate the activation energy for the diffusion of nickel in this alloy over this temperature range. Give your answer as the value of activation_energy.The unit of the answer is kJ/mol.
response:
Using the Arrhenius relation $D = D_0 \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{Q}{RT}\right)$, with the two data points:

$$\ln\!\frac{D_2}{D_1} = \frac{Q}{R}\!\left(\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2}\right)$$

where $T_1 = 773\,\text{K}$, $T_2 = 1273\,\text{K}$, $D_1=10^{-22}$, $D_2=10^{-15}$:

$$Q = \frac{R\ln(D_2/D_1)}{1/T_1 - 1/T_2} \approx 2.637\times10^{5}\,\text{J/mol} \approx 263.7\,\text{kJ/mol}$$

$$\boxed{263.7}$$
